Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Money, work & business

estimate verb and noun

also estimate the cost, rough estimate, valuation, work out roughly

classical

Cic. Dom. 44 (Lewis & Short): domum ēmit prope dīmidiō cārius quam aestimābat
Catull. 5.3: omnēs ūnius aestimēmus assis
Traupman 323

aestimō, aestimāre, aestimāvī, aestimātum

verb, first conjugation, transitive; the value in the genitive or ablative

estimate, value, put a figure on

Lewis & Short: “to determine or estimate the extrinsic (money) value of a thing, to value, rate, appraise”. For “think, reckon”, use exīstimāre or putāre, which Lewis & Short sets apart from it.

Other words

  • ratiōnem inīre — work out, make an estimate

    verb phrase; ineō, irregular · also used · classical · Cato Agr. 2.2 (Lewis & Short): ratiōnem inīre oportet operārum, diērum

    Lewis & Short: “to make an estimate”. For a rough figure Latin adds circiter or ferē. Lewis & Short: “to cast up, reckon, calculate” (Caes. BG 7.71.4); Traupman also uses it for “take steps, take measures”, which we have not found in Lewis & Short.

  • aestimātiō, aestimātiōnis f. — an estimate, a valuation

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Liv. 39.6.9: vīlissimum antīquīs mancipium et aestimātiōne et ūsū

Examples

  • rūmōrēsque senum sevēriōrum omnēs ūnius aestimēmus assis

    and let us value all the gossip of stern old men at a single pennyCatull. 5.2–3

  • tum coquus, vīlissimum antīquīs mancipium et aestimātiōne et ūsū, in pretiō esse, et quod ministerium fuerat, ars habērī coepta

    Then the cook, to our forefathers the cheapest of slaves both in value and in use, began to be prized, and what had been a menial job came to be thought an art.Liv. 39.6.9

  • Quantī aestimās hanc domum?

    What do you think this house is worth?composed

  • ratiōnem inīre

    to take steps, to take measuresTraupman 385

See also value, price, how much is it?.
